info.title: MSP API
info.description: Multi-sport competition platform. Errors are Problem Details with a stable `code` (contracts/errors.json) and the request's `correlationId`.

get.summary: Get a media file by its signed URL
get.description: Serves one stored file of a media asset while its signed URL is valid (10 minutes). Only signed URLs from an admin read lead here; the token names the tenant, the asset and the variant. Photo variants are served inline; documents (the original, whatever its type) as a download. `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

The tenant whose site this host serves: slug, display name and primary domain. The tenant comes from the request host (`X-Forwarded-Host` from a trusted proxy). Responses differ per host. Cacheable for a minute; send the `ETag` back as `If-None-Match` to get 304.
Active ISO 3166-1 countries, ordered by alpha-2 code. Cacheable for an hour; send the `ETag` back as `If-None-Match` to get 304.
Active ISO 4217 currencies (money only), ordered by code, with their minor units. Cacheable for an hour; send the `ETag` back as `If-None-Match` to get 304.
Active ISO 639-1 languages, ordered by code. Cacheable for an hour; send the `ETag` back as `If-None-Match` to get 304.

Active IANA time zones, ordered by ID. `country` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, upper case) keeps only that country's zones; a country without zones gives an empty list. Cacheable for an hour; send the `ETag` back as `If-None-Match` to get 304.

get.summary: Get a person on the public site
get.description: A person of the tenant whose site this host serves, when the person is active, their public profile is on and, for a person who is a minor or whose age is unknown, a guardian's consent with `PUBLIC_PROFILE` is in force; otherwise PERSON_NOT_FOUND. An adult shows nationality, the photo and active athlete profiles (codes; labels from the sport's definition); anyone else only the display name, and the photo with `PHOTO` consent. `photo` holds the photo route's paths. Cacheable for a minute; send the `ETag` back as `If-None-Match` to get 304.

get.summary: Get a person's photo on the public site
get.description: A variant (`THUMBNAIL` 160 px, `MEDIUM` 640 px, `LARGE` 1600 px on the longest side; required) of the photo of a person the public read shows, as WebP. Checked as the public read is, on every request: a person it doesn't show is PERSON_NOT_FOUND, one shown without a photo (none, or no `PHOTO` consent for a minor) PERSON_PHOTO_NOT_FOUND. `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`.

patch.description: Changes the keys sent of the settings of the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id`; missing or null keys stay as they are. Any other key, or a value of the wrong type, is 400 VALIDATION_INVALID_REQUEST with an `errors` entry naming it. Send `version` from the last read to get 409 TENANT_CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT instead of overwriting someone else's change; `If-Match` with the `ETag` works the same way (if both are sent, both must match).

get.description: The status and access mode of the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id`, with the reason and time of the change that put it in that status, the tenant's time zone, and the current subscription period's status and days (`null` without a period). Available while the tenant is suspended or archived, so its owner sees why every other request is `403 TENANT_BLOCKED`, and while it is read-only, when writes are `403 TENANT_READ_ONLY`.

The subscription of the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id`: the current period (plan, kind, status today and days, all in the tenant's time zone; `null` without a period; with none started, the earliest scheduled one) and the next: the earliest period that starts after today and after the current one, never the current one; every entitlement's value today with its source (DEFAULT, PLAN or OVERRIDE); and every quota's usage (`used` of `limit`, `null` = unlimited; `warning` from 80 % of the limit; `measured: false` while no module counts it yet). Available while the tenant is read-only. To change the plan, the tenant contacts the platform.

get.summary: List the sport variants and which the tenant has enabled
get.description: Every published sport variant (latest version) with its sport, name and scoring family, and whether the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id` has it enabled (`enabledSince`: when its current enablement began). `sportQuota` is the usage of MAX_ENABLED_SPORTS (distinct sports, not variants; `limit` `null` = unlimited; `warning` from 80 % of the limit) for those who may read the subscription, else `null`. Available while the tenant is read-only.

post.summary: Enable a sport variant for the tenant
post.description: `variant` is a published variant's code (GET /api/admin/v1/sports), matched exactly; another is TENANT_SPORT_VARIANT_UNKNOWN on the field `variant`. The plan's MAX_ENABLED_SPORTS counts distinct sports: a variant of a sport the tenant already has adds nothing and is never refused for it; another sport at the limit is ENTITLEMENT_QUOTA_EXCEEDED ("Your plan allows N sports."). An enabled variant is TENANT_SPORT_ALREADY_ENABLED. Enabling a variant that was disabled adds a new enablement; the earlier ones are kept.

post.summary: Disable a sport variant for the tenant
post.description: `variant` is a published variant's code (GET /api/admin/v1/sports), matched exactly; another is TENANT_SPORT_VARIANT_UNKNOWN on the field `variant`. Ends the variant's enablement now, with `reason`; nothing that uses the variant changes, and lowering the sport quota never disables a sport. A variant that isn't enabled is TENANT_SPORT_NOT_ENABLED. The reason is kept permanently on the enablement and in the audit trail: don't include personal data.

post.summary: Invite a person to the tenant
post.description: Invites `email` to join the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id` with `roleCodes` (tenant roles, tenant-wide). Only an owner invites with TENANT_OWNER or replaces a pending invitation that has it. A person who is already a member (active or suspended) can't be invited. Every member who isn't removed and every pending invitation takes one of the plan's staff users (MAX_STAFF_USERS); an invitation past the limit is ENTITLEMENT_QUOTA_EXCEEDED, and one that replaces a pending invitation to the same email adds no one. The invitation lasts 7 days; the email with its link goes out shortly after (one link at a time: a resent email's link replaces the earlier one). A pending invitation to the same email is revoked and replaced.

ETag.description: The resource's `version`, quoted (a strong entity tag). Send it back as `If-Match`.

Sending its email changes its version, so a revoke may get 409 once while the email goes out. The body is optional. Returns the invitation. Send `version` or `If-Match` from the last read to get 409 AUTH_CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT if the invitation changed since.

get.summary: List the tenant actions the signed-in user may perform, and those the tenant can't use now
get.description: What the signed-in user's roles grant in the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id` (tenant actions, docs/generated/actions.md). Without `scopeType`/`scopeId`, the actions granted tenant-wide; with them (COMPETITION, TEAM or CONTEST and its ID), also those granted on that resource or the scopes above it. `actions`: what the user may perform now, in ordinal order. `unavailable`: what the roles grant but the tenant can't use now, each with the refusal a request would get: TENANT_READ_ONLY (the subscription has ended, was cancelled or hasn't started) or ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED (with the entitlement and the plans that include it, for "Requires PRO plan"). Actions the roles don't grant are in neither list. `access`: the tenant's access mode, the current subscription period's status and last days (null without a period) and the tenant's time zone, for the banner. The admin app shows only what `actions` allows and disables what `unavailable` lists; every request is still authorized. A read-only tenant answers this request; a blocked one, or a provisioning one for a member who can't set it up, answers 403 with the reason (TENANT_BLOCKED, TENANT_PROVISIONING).

A published version never changes. Labels are the definition's; show them as given. Not audited (global configuration).

ETag.description: The definition's `contentHash`, quoted: it changes only with a new version.

post.description:
Resolves the ruleset template `code` at `version` (the latest when left out) with one of its formats and the changes a competition would make, into the effective-rules snapshot an edition would freeze (docs/domain/rulesets.md): the exact sport, format and template versions, the format's parameters with their defaults, the rules and the snapshot's `hash`. The same template version, format version, parameters and changes always give the same hash. `overrides` is keyed by the template's editable paths (`standings.points.win`); paths left out keep the template's values. Nothing is saved or audited.

A rule or parameter the resolver refuses is 422 with the first problem's code (by field) and one `errors` entry per field: `format.code`, `format.version`, `format.parameters.<code>`, `overrides.<path>`. A value that isn't a whole number, true or false, a code or a list of codes is refused on its field like a value of the wrong type, or as an unknown path when the template has no such editable path. A missing format or format code, a `format.version` below 1, or another member is 400 VALIDATION_INVALID_REQUEST.

get.description: The people of the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id`, sorted by last name, first name and ID. `q` matches a name or an alias by prefix or similarity (in any order: "Ssekandi John" finds John Ssekandi) and an external identifier's value exactly. Filter by `status` (without it, archived people are left out) and `ageStatus` (on the tenant's date; UNKNOWN: no date of birth); `profile` and `variant` keep people with a profile of that kind and sport variant that isn't archived: an athlete profile's variant or one of a staff or official profile's capabilities (a variant without people answers an empty page). `limit` is 1–100 (25). Items carry the birth year, never the date of birth. `isMinor` is true unless the person is known to be an adult (`ageStatus` UNKNOWN: true).

post.summary: Add a person after a duplicate check
post.description: Adds an ACTIVE person to the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id`. Run the duplicate check first with the same names, date of birth, nationalities and external identifiers, and send its `checkToken`: without one, or with one that is expired (30 minutes), for other details or another user, the create is PERSON_DUPLICATE_CHECK_REQUIRED. The check runs again: an external identifier another person holds is PERSON_EXTERNAL_ID_EXISTS; a person the check didn't answer (added since) is PERSON_DUPLICATE_CHECK_STALE (check again); people it answered need `overrideReason` (PERSON_DUPLICATE_OVERRIDE_REQUIRED), and each is then remembered as not the same person, so the check doesn't show the pair again. A first or last name without a letter or a digit is PERSON_NAME_INVALID; a date of birth after the tenant's date is PERSON_DATE_OF_BIRTH_IN_FUTURE; the authorities NATIONAL_ID, NIN and PASSPORT are PERSON_EXTERNAL_ID_AUTHORITY_RESERVED. The reason is kept permanently on the decisions and in the audit trail: don't include personal data. Answers the person as GET /people/{personId} does.

ETag.description: The resource's `version`, quoted (a strong entity tag). Send it back as `If-Match`.

post.summary: Check a person against the registry for duplicates
post.description: Compares a new or changed person with the people of the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id`, whatever their status, and answers those who may be the same person, strongest first, at most 20. `EXACT_IDENTIFIER`: an external identifier with the same authority and value. `LIKELY`: the same date of birth and the same names in any order, or names at least 80 % similar. `POSSIBLE`: names at least 60 % similar and a date of birth missing, birth years within one year or a nationality in common (primary or secondary, on either side); the same names with another date of birth; or the same date of birth and last name. Names are also compared with aliases. `evidence` says why; it never carries the other person's date of birth. With `personId` (a person being changed), that person and everyone already decided "not the same person" as them are left out. Nothing is saved; `checkToken` (valid 30 minutes, for these details and this user) is what creating the person needs. A first or last name without a letter or a digit is PERSON_NAME_INVALID; a date of birth after the tenant's date is PERSON_DATE_OF_BIRTH_IN_FUTURE; the authorities NATIONAL_ID, NIN and PASSPORT are PERSON_EXTERNAL_ID_AUTHORITY_RESERVED. Nationalities are active countries of the reference data.

get.description: A person of the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id`, whatever their status: names, aliases, external identifiers, the birth year, `isMinor` and `ageStatus` on the tenant's date, and `version` (also the `ETag`). The date of birth is in the private read. `isMinor` is true unless the person is known to be an adult: without a date of birth, `ageStatus` is UNKNOWN and `isMinor` is true. `photo` holds signed URLs of the photo's three sizes, working until `expiresAt` (read the person again for new ones; never cache them), or is null.

ETag.description: The resource's `version`, quoted (a strong entity tag). Send it back as `If-Match`.

put.description: Replaces the biodata of a person of the tenant named by `X-Tenant-Id`, whatever their status: a field left out is cleared. External identifiers and aliases have their own actions; the status changes through the lifecycle actions. When the names (as the duplicate check compares them: case, accents and punctuation aside), the date of birth or the nationalities change, run the duplicate check for the new details with `personId` and no external identifiers, and send its `checkToken`; then it works as a create does: PERSON_DUPLICATE_CHECK_REQUIRED, PERSON_DUPLICATE_CHECK_STALE, and `overrideReason` for the people it found (PERSON_DUPLICATE_OVERRIDE_REQUIRED), each then remembered as not the same person. People already decided not the same person as this one aren't found again. Send `version` or `If-Match` from the last read to get 409 PERSON_CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT if the person changed since. The reason is kept permanently on the decisions and in the audit trail: don't include personal data. Answers the person as GET /people/{personId} does.

post.description: Adds another name the person is known by (`FORMER_NAME`, `NICKNAME` or `SPELLING`): the directory search and the duplicate check find the person under it too. No duplicate check runs. A name the person is already known by (the same name key as their own name or a current alias: word order, case, accents and punctuation aside) is PERSON_ALIAS_EXISTS; a name without a letter or a digit PERSON_NAME_INVALID. An archived or deceased person takes no new alias (PERSON_ARCHIVED, PERSON_DECEASED). put.description: Uploads a photo as `multipart/form-data` with one file in the field `file` and nothing else (VALIDATION_INVALID_REQUEST otherwise). The file's bytes decide its type, not the content type sent: JPEG, PNG or WebP up to 5 MB (MEDIA_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED, MEDIA_TOO_LARGE; an image that can't be decoded or is over 40 megapixels is MEDIA_IMAGE_UNREADABLE). It is stored as WebP at 160, 640 and 1600 px on the longest side, without its metadata (a GPS position, the camera), and replaces the photo the person had. At the plan's storage limit the upload is ENTITLEMENT_QUOTA_EXCEEDED ("Your plan allows N GB of storage."). An archived or deceased person takes no new photo (PERSON_ARCHIVED, PERSON_DECEASED). Send `If-Match` from the last read to get 409 PERSON_CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT if the person changed since. Answers the person as GET /people/{personId} does; its version moves.

post.description: ACTIVE or SUSPENDED → ARCHIVED, with a reason. Its data and slug are kept; the slug is never reused. The body `{ "reason": … }` is required (no body: VALIDATION_MALFORMED_REQUEST). The reason is kept permanently in the status history and the audit trail: don't include personal data. Send `version` or `If-Match` from the last read to get 409 TENANT_CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT if the tenant changed since.

post.description: ARCHIVED → SUSPENDED, with a reason; restore it as a separate step. The body `{ "reason": … }` is required (no body: VALIDATION_MALFORMED_REQUEST). The reason is kept permanently in the status history and the audit trail: don't include personal data. Send `version` or `If-Match` from the last read to get 409 TENANT_CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT if the tenant changed since.

get.description: Every subscription period of the tenant, latest start first, with its status on `today` (the tenant's date), the current period (the one that decides access; with none started, the earliest scheduled one) and the next: the earliest period that starts after today and after the current one, never the current one. Statuses are derived from the dates: SCHEDULED, ACTIVE, EXPIRING, GRACE, EXPIRED or CANCELLED.

post.summary: Give a tenant a subscription period
post.description: A new period on `planCode` (an active plan; otherwise TENANT_PLAN_NOT_FOUND on the field) from `startsOn` to `endsOn`. Dates are the tenant's (its time zone in settings) and both `startsOn` and `endsOn` are included. `kind` (PAID, TRIAL or COMPLIMENTARY) is for reporting only. `expiringWindowDays` defaults to 30 and `graceDays` to 14 (0–365). A period that shares a day with another period that isn't cancelled is refused (TENANT_SUBSCRIPTION_OVERLAP). A trial, an event pass or the pilot offer is an ordinary period.

A new period from the day after the latest period (that isn't cancelled) ends, or from today if that day has passed or every period is cancelled, to `endsOn`. Dates are the tenant's (its time zone in settings) and both `startsOn` and `endsOn` are included. `planCode`, `kind` and the windows not sent are the latest period's: a lower plan is chosen here. Without any period, TENANT_SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND (assign one instead); an `endsOn` before the first day, VALIDATION_INVALID_REQUEST on `endsOn`; no `planCode` while the latest period's plan is no longer active, TENANT_PLAN_NOT_FOUND on `planCode`.

post.summary: Move a tenant to a higher plan now
post.description: Cancels the current period (reason "Changed to <plan>") and adds one on `planCode` from today to the same `endsOn`, with the same kind and windows; the history keeps both. Only to a higher plan (TENANT_SUBSCRIPTION_DOWNGRADE_AT_RENEWAL otherwise: choose a lower plan when renewing), and only while the current period is ACTIVE or EXPIRING (TENANT_SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND otherwise: renew instead).

Cancels, now and with `reason`, every period that isn't cancelled or expired: those in effect today (an earlier one still in GRACE included) and every scheduled one. Nothing to cancel is TENANT_SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND. The reason is kept permanently on the periods and in the audit trail: don't include personal data.

post.summary: Give a tenant its own value of an entitlement
post.description: `value` in place of the plan's for `entitlementCode` (a declared entitlement, GET /api/platform/v1/plans), of its type: `{"enabled": true}`, `{"limit": 5}` (`null` = unlimited) or `{"level": "FULL"}` (`null` = none); otherwise TENANT_OVERRIDE_INVALID_VALUE on the field. It applies until `effectiveUntil` (the tenant's date, included; on or after its today, else VALIDATION_INVALID_REQUEST on the field) or, without one, until it is removed. An override already in place for the entitlement is removed ("Replaced by a new override") in the same change; the history keeps both. The reason is kept permanently on the override and in the audit trail, and tenants never see it: don't include personal data.

Removes the override now, with `reason`: the plan's value applies again. An override the tenant doesn't have, or one already removed (or replaced), is TENANT_OVERRIDE_NOT_FOUND. The reason is kept permanently on the override and in the audit trail, and tenants never see it: don't include personal data.

get.description: The active plans in rank order (then by code), each with every entitlement's definition and value, ordered by entitlement code. A value is `{ enabled }`, `{ limit }` (null = unlimited) or `{ level }` (null = none); `value` itself is null when the configuration seed hasn't written that entitlement yet (not "unlimited"). Plans change only through a reviewed seed (no editing). Every read is audited.

get.summary: List the platform actions the signed-in user may perform
get.description: The codes of the platform actions (docs/generated/actions.md) the signed-in user's platform roles grant, in ordinal order. The platform console shows only what this list allows; every request is still authorized.

Every published sport variant at its latest version, ordered by name, then variant code: its sport, scoring family, contest shape and latest version. Not paginated. Not audited (global configuration).

A variant's published definition (docs/domain/sports/README.md) at `version`, the latest when left out: terminology, periods, actor roles, event types and the generic event types every definition has, positions, staff and official roles, lineup, statistics and the scorer pad. A published version never changes. Labels are the definition's; show them as given. Not audited (global configuration).

ETag.description: The definition's `contentHash`, quoted: it changes only with a new version.

get.description: Every published format at its latest version, ordered by name, then code, in full: compatible contest shapes, participant range, stages and their generators, and the parameters with type, bounds and default. Not paginated. Not audited (global configuration).

A published format (docs/domain/formats.md) at `version`, the latest when left out: compatible contest shapes, participant range, stages and their generators, and the parameters with type, bounds and default. A published version never changes. Not audited (global configuration).

ETag.description: The format's `contentHash`, quoted: it changes only with a new version.

get.description: Every published ruleset template at its latest version, ordered by name, then code, in full: the sport variant and version, the formats, the rules, the parameters a competition may change (type, bounds or values, default) and the tiebreakers they name. Not paginated. Not audited (global configuration).

A published ruleset template (docs/domain/rulesets.md) at `version`, the latest when left out: the sport variant and version, the formats, the rules, the parameters a competition may change (type, bounds or values, default) and the tiebreakers they name. A published version never changes. Not audited (global configuration).

ETag.description: The template's `contentHash`, quoted: it changes only with a new version.

post.description: Signs in with email and password and starts a session: the response sets the session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict; 12 hours sliding, 7 days at most). An unknown email, a wrong password, a locked or unconfirmed account all answer `AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS`. Five wrong passwords lock the account for 15 minutes. Limited to 20 attempts a minute per client address and 10 per 15 minutes per email (`AUTH_RATE_LIMITED`, with `Retry-After`). Needs `X-CSRF: 1` like every other change.
Ends this session and deletes the session cookie.

get.description: The signed-in user: ID, email, active platform roles, and the tenants they are an active member of, ordered by name, each with its slug, display name and status and the user's roles there. Every status is listed. A suspended or archived tenant's workspace is blocked (TENANT_BLOCKED): only `tenant.access.read` is allowed. A provisioning tenant's workspace opens only for those setting it up; others get TENANT_PROVISIONING.

post.summary: Ask for a password reset email
post.description: Sends a password reset link to the email if it belongs to an account. Always answers 202, whether or not it does. The link works once, for 1 hour, and only the newest link works. Limited to 10 requests an hour per client address and 3 an hour per email (`AUTH_RATE_LIMITED`, with `Retry-After`). Needs `X-CSRF: 1`.

post.summary: Set a new password with a reset token
post.description: Sets a new password with the token from a reset email's link. The token works once, for 1 hour, and only the newest one works; otherwise `AUTH_RESET_TOKEN_INVALID`. The new password needs at least 12 characters (`AUTH_PASSWORD_REJECTED`, the rule in `detail`). Signs out every session of the user and clears a lockout; it does not sign in. Needs `X-CSRF: 1`.

Changes the signed-in user's password. A wrong current password answers `AUTH_CURRENT_PASSWORD_INVALID` and counts toward the lockout (five lock the account for 15 minutes). The new password needs at least 12 characters (`AUTH_PASSWORD_REJECTED`, the rule in `detail`). The user's other sessions end within 5 minutes; this one stays (the response renews its cookie). Needs `X-CSRF: 1`.

post.summary: Look up an invitation by its token
post.description: What an invitation link is for: the tenant, the invited email and roles, when it expires, and whether the email has an account (then sign in with it before accepting; otherwise choose a password when accepting). The token from the email's link goes in the body. An unknown, revoked or replaced token is `AUTH_INVITATION_TOKEN_INVALID`; an expired invitation `AUTH_INVITATION_EXPIRED`; an accepted one `AUTH_INVITATION_ALREADY_ACCEPTED`. Anonymous callers allowed; needs `X-CSRF: 1`.

Joins the invitation's tenant with its roles. If the invited email has no account, send `password` (at least 12 characters, `AUTH_PASSWORD_REJECTED`): the account is created with that password. If it has one, sign in with it first (`AUTH_INVITATION_SIGN_IN_REQUIRED` otherwise); `password` is then ignored. The token works once and the same refusals as the lookup apply; a current member gets `AUTH_ALREADY_MEMBER`. Does not sign in. Anonymous callers allowed; needs `X-CSRF: 1`.

AcceptInvitationRequest.description:
The token from an invitation email's link, and the password to set when the invited email has no account yet
(ignored when it has one: the invitee is signed in as that user instead).

AcceptInvitationResponse.description: The membership the invitee now holds; they sign in to use it (accepting doesn't sign in).

ActorPool.description: Who may fill an actor role.

ActorSide.description: Whose side, relative to the event's side.

AddExternalIdentifierRequest.description:
A new external identifier of a person (S06 D10): the authority's code, its value, and since when it is valid;
`version`, when sent, must be the person's current one.

AddPersonAliasRequest.description:
A new alias (S06 D10): the name as the person is known by it and its kind; `version`, when sent, must be the
person's current one.

AgeStatus.description:
Whether a person is an adult on the tenant's date (S06 D13): computed from the date of birth on every read, never
stored. AgeStatus.Unknown means no date of birth is recorded; such a person is treated as a minor wherever data
is shown publicly.

AssignmentScope.description: A role assignment scope that can grant a tenant action.

AssignPeriodRequest.description:
A new period: `planCode` from `startsOn` to `endsOn` (both included, the tenant's dates). The windows
default to 30 expiring and 14 grace days.

AssignRoleRequest.description:
A role to give a member: its code and scope (`TENANT` when not sent; the only scope S03 accepts, so
`scopeId` stays empty). `version`, when sent, must be the membership's current one.

AthleteProfileResponse.description:
A sport variant the person plays (S06 D12): codes of the variant's definition (its labels come from
`GET /sports/{variant}`, AR-29). `publicName` as recorded: null shows the display name.

AuditEntryResponse.description:
One audit entry as platform staff see it: every column, with `metadata` as the JSON object it was stored as
(personal data already masked when it was recorded).

CancelSubscriptionRequest.description:
The body of `subscription.cancel` (audit `REQUIRED_WITH_REASON`). The reason is kept permanently on the
cancelled periods and in the audit trail and is not redacted: it must not contain personal data.

CandidateIdentifier.description: An external identifier of the person to check: the authority's code and the value it gave.

CapabilitiesResponse.description:
The platform action codes the caller may perform, in ordinal order; Scope is always null (kept so
the platform list has the shape it had in S03). The tenant list is TenantCapabilitiesResponse.

CapabilityAccessResponse.description:
The tenant's access today, for the shell's banner: the access `mode`; the current subscription period's status,
first day, last day, last day of grace and the day it was cancelled (all null without a period; `cancelledOn`
null unless it was cancelled), so the banner can say since when a tenant is read-only; the tenant's `timeZone`
(IANA), in which the days begin and end. A response of its own, so a field added to Tenancy's contract doesn't change
the API.

CapabilityScopeResponse.description: The resource the capabilities were asked about.

ChangeMemberStatusRequest.description: The optional body of `restore`: `version`, when sent, must be the membership's current one.

ChangeMemberStatusWithReasonRequest.description:
The body of `suspend` and `remove` (audit `REQUIRED_WITH_REASON`). The reason is kept permanently on
the membership and in the audit trail and is not redacted: it must not contain personal data.

ChangePersonStatusRequest.description:
The optional body of `deactivate` and `reactivate`: an optional reason, kept in the status history and the
audit trail and not redacted, so it must not contain personal data; `version`, when sent, must be the person's
current one.

ChangePersonStatusWithReasonRequest.description:
The body of `archive`, `unarchive` and `mark-deceased` (audit `REQUIRED_WITH_REASON`). The reason
is kept permanently in the status history and the audit trail and is not redacted: it must not contain personal data.

ChangePlanRequest.description: The higher plan to move to now.

ChangeProfileStatusRequest.description:
A profile's new status, with a reason (audit `REQUIRED_WITH_REASON`). The reason is kept permanently in the
profile's history and the audit trail and is not redacted: it must not contain personal data.

ChangeTenantStatusRequest.description: The optional body of `activate` and `restore`: `version`, when sent, must be the tenant's current one.

ChangeTenantStatusWithReasonRequest.description:
The body of `suspend`, `archive` and `unarchive` (audit `REQUIRED_WITH_REASON`). The reason is kept
permanently in the status history and the audit trail and is not redacted: it must not contain personal data.

CheckDuplicatesRequest.description:
The person to check (S06 D5): the names, date of birth, nationalities and external identifiers a create or an update
would save. `personId` names the person being changed (S06 D8): that person is left out, and so is everyone
already decided "not the same person" as them (S06 D7).

CheckDuplicatesResponse.description:
The duplicate check's answer (S06 D5): the existing people who may be the same person, strongest first, at most 20,
and the token a create needs (S06 D6). It carries no `PRIVATE` value: a birth year, never a date of birth.

CheckVenueDuplicatesRequest.description: What the venue duplicate warning compares (S07 D13): the name, the city and the coordinates a save would send.

CheckVenueDuplicatesResponse.description: The venues that look like the one checked, strongest first (none is an empty list).

ConsentEvidenceResponse.description:
The evidence's signed URL (S06 D17): it downloads the file until `expiresAt` (ten minutes with the local
storage); read again for a new one. Never cache it.

ConsentPrivateResponse.description: A consent's guardian and evidence (S06 D14).

ConsentScope.description: What a guardian consents to (S06 D14, ADR-0015).

ConsentStatus.description: A consent record's states (S06 D14, Q39; docs/domain/state-machines.md, Registry).

CountryResponse.description: An ISO 3166-1 country: alpha-2 `code` (`UG`), alpha-3, numeric code and English name.

CoverageLevel.description: In order: a level includes every level before it.

CreateAthleteProfileRequest.description:
A new athlete profile (S06 D12): the variant's code, then the details as UpdateAthleteProfileRequest
takes them; `version`, when sent, must be the person's current one.

CreatePersonRequest.description:
A new person (S06 D2, D6): the biodata, external identifiers, the duplicate check's token for the same details, and
the reason to proceed past the people the check found.

CreateTenantRequest.description:
A new tenant. Every field but `publicEnabled` (default false) is required; unknown members are rejected,
so a status can't be sent (a new tenant is always `PROVISIONING`).

CreateVenueRequest.description:
A new venue (S07 D3): its fields, an optional slug (proposed from the name when none is sent, D9), and, after the
duplicate warning, `duplicatesReviewed` with an optional reason (D13).

CurrencyResponse.description: An ISO 4217 currency: alphabetic `code` (`UGX`), numeric code, English name, minor units (UGX 0).

DisableSportRequest.description:
The body of `tenant.sport.disable` (audit `REQUIRED_WITH_REASON`). The reason is kept permanently on the
enablement and in the audit trail and is not redacted: it must not contain personal data.

DuplicateCandidateResponse.description:
A person who matched. `EXACT_IDENTIFIER` blocks creation; `LIKELY` and `POSSIBLE` need a reason to
proceed. `status` marks an archived, inactive or deceased person. `athleteVariants`: the sport variants of
their athlete profiles that aren't archived, by code (S06 D5).

DuplicateConfidence.description: How sure the duplicate check is that an existing person is the candidate (S06 D5), weakest first.

DuplicateEvidenceCode.description:
Why a person matched. The answer never carries the other person's date of birth; `SAME_DATE_OF_BIRTH` confirms
a date the caller already sent.

DuplicateEvidenceResponse.description:
Why the person matched. `value`: the authority for `SAME_EXTERNAL_ID`, the whole percentage for
`NAME_SIMILARITY`, otherwise null.

EffectiveEntitlementResponse.description:
A tenant's value of one entitlement today and where it comes from: `DEFAULT`, `PLAN` (the current period's
plan) or `OVERRIDE` (an unremoved override in effect).

EndExternalIdentifierRequest.description:
The end of an external identifier: `validTo` defaults to the tenant's today. The optional reason is kept in the
audit trail and is not redacted: it must not contain personal data.

EntitlementOverrideResponse.description:
One entitlement override: `value` in place of the plan's for `entitlementCode`, until `effectiveUntil`
(included; none = until removed). `inEffect`: it applies on the response's `today` (not removed, not past
its last day). The removal fields are set together.

EntitlementSource.description: Where a tenant's effective value of an entitlement comes from (S04 D6).

EntitlementType.description: What kind of value an entitlement has (docs/architecture/authorization.md, "Entitlements").

limit.description: QUOTA: the most items; null = unlimited.

level.description: LEVEL: a level code; null = none.

EntitlementValue.description: An entitlement's value, by its type: `{ enabled }` (BOOLEAN), `{ limit }` (QUOTA; null = unlimited) or `{ level }` (LEVEL; null = none).

ExternalIdentifierResponse.description: An identifier another authority gave the person; one with `validTo` has ended (S06 D10).

ForfeitScoreResponse.description: The score recorded for a forfeit (the file's `for` and `against`).

ForgotPasswordRequest.description: Ask for a password reset email.

FormatDefinitionResponse.description:
A published format as the API shows it (docs/domain/formats.md): camelCase names, UPPER_SNAKE values, with its
version's hash and publication time. Parameters stay a map keyed by their codes, as in the file (`cycles`).

FormatParameterResponse.description:
A parameter: `min` and `max` for a number, `values` for a choice (empty otherwise); `default` is
the bare value (a whole number, true or false, or one of the values).

FormatParameterType.description: A parameter's type in the API (`CHOICE`, `FLAG`, `NUMBER`); the files write `enum`, `bool`, `int`.

FormatParticipantsResponse.description: How many participants the format takes, both ends included.

GrantOverrideRequest.description:
The body of `entitlement.override` (audit `REQUIRED_WITH_REASON`): `value` in place of the plan's for
`entitlementCode`, until `effectiveUntil` (the tenant's date, included; none = until removed). The reason
is kept permanently in the override and the audit trail and is not redacted: it must not contain personal data.

InvitationResponse.description:
An invitation as the admin API shows it. `status` is `EXPIRED` for a pending one past `expiresAt`. The
email is shown to every holder of `membership.read`, like a member's (owner, S03-T4b), and never logged or
audited. `version` (also the `ETag`) changes whenever the invitation does, a resent email included.

InvitationState.description:
An invitation as people see it: the stored status, with InvitationState.Expired derived from a pending invitation's
`expires_at` (S03 D12). Never stored.

InviteMemberRequest.description: Invite a person to the tenant: their email and the tenant roles they get, tenant-wide.

LanguageResponse.description: An ISO 639-1 language: two-letter `code` (`sw`) and English name.

LoginRequest.description: Sign in with email and password.

LookupInvitationRequest.description: The token from an invitation email's link, in the body so request logs and traces never hold it.

LookupInvitationResponse.description:
A pending invitation as its invitee sees it: the tenant's display name, the invited email (the token proves the
invitee holds it), the tenant-wide roles, when it expires, and whether the email has an account: if it does, the
invitee signs in with it before accepting; if not, they choose a password when accepting.

MemberResponse.description:
A member of the tenant as the admin API shows them, with their active roles. The email is the user's only
identifier until people have profiles; shown to every holder of `membership.read` (owner, S03-T4b) and never
logged or audited. `version` (also the `ETag`) is the membership's; role changes change it too.

MemberRoleResponse.description: An active role assignment: the role, where it applies (`scopeId` null tenant-wide) and when it was granted.

MeResponse.description: The signed-in user: their own email, platform roles and the tenants they are an active member of.

MeTenantResponse.description:
A tenant the user is an active member of: its slug (the workspace URL), display name and status, and the codes of the
roles they hold there (any scope). Every status is listed. A `SUSPENDED` or `ARCHIVED` tenant's workspace is
blocked, and its owner can read why; a `PROVISIONING` tenant's opens only for those setting it up (others get
`TENANT_PROVISIONING`).

MinorConsentRequirement.description: Whether a minor needs a guardian's consent to take part; the registry slices add the others.

MinorRegistrationConsent.description:
Whether a guardian's consent is needed before a minor is registered for a competition (Q11). Consent before public
exposure is always required, whatever this says.

NewExternalIdentifier.description: An external identifier of the new person: the authority's code, its value, and since when it is valid.

OfficialCapabilityRequest.description:
One official capability as sent: a variant's code, an official role code of its definition, and an optional grade,
licence number and licence end date (each optional on its own).

OfficialCapabilityResponse.description:
One thing an official does: a variant, an official role of its definition, the grade and licence recorded.
`licenceExpired` is true when `licenceValidUntil` is before the tenant's today (a licence is valid through
its last day; without a date it never expires). Nothing is refused for an expired licence in S06.

OfficialProfileRequest.description:
An official profile's capabilities, for a new profile or replacing a profile's as a whole (S06 D12): 1–10, one per
variant and role. `version`, when sent, must be the person's current one.

OfficialProfileResponse.description:
A person's work as an official (S06 D12): what they officiate as, by variant and role (codes of the variant's
definition; labels from `GET /sports/{variant}`, AR-29).

OutboxMessageResponse.description:
One outbox message in the platform diagnostics: envelope and delivery state, no payload. `heldBackBy` is set on
a `PENDING` message that waits for an earlier, not yet processed message of its aggregate.

OutboxMessageStatus.description: Delivery status of an outbox message (docs/domain/state-machines.md, "Outbox message").

PageInfo.description:
The `page` member of a cursor-paginated list (docs/architecture/api-conventions.md): pass
NextCursor as `cursor` to get the next page; it is null on the last page.

ParameterValue.description: A parameter's value, by the parameter's type: a whole number (NUMBER), true or false (FLAG), one of its values (CHOICE), or an ordered list of its values, each once (LIST).

PersonListItem.description:
A person in the directory (S06 D22). `person.read` answers `INTERNAL` and `PUBLIC` fields only: the
birth year, `isMinor` and `ageStatus` on the tenant's date, never the date of birth (S06 D3, D13).
`isMinor` is true unless the person is known to be an adult: a person without a date of birth
(`UNKNOWN`) is treated as a minor.

PersonPhotoResponse.description:
A person's photo as signed URLs, one per size (S06 D17): 160, 640 and 1600 px on the longest side, WebP. They work
until `expiresAt` (ten minutes with the local storage); read the person again for new ones. Never cache them.

PersonPrivateResponse.description:
A person's `PRIVATE` data, for `person.read_private` (S06 D3): the full date of birth, and the guardian
and the evidence of every consent, withdrawn ones included (matched to `consents` of the person read by ID).

PersonResponse.description:
A person's record as `person.read` shows it (S06 D3, D22): no `PRIVATE` field. Aliases are the ones not
removed; athlete profiles are all of them, archived ones included, by variant; staff and official profiles all of
them, archived ones included, oldest first. `photo` holds short-lived URLs (S06 D17), null without a photo.
`version` is also the `ETag`;
a change to an alias, an identifier or a profile changes it too (S06 D11).

PersonSource.description: Where a record came from (AR-22). Imports add their own value with Data Exchange.

PersonStatus.description: A person's stored states in S06 (docs/domain/state-machines.md, Registry; `MERGED` comes with merges, S25).

PersonStatusChangeResponse.description: One row of a person's status history (S06 D9): `fromStatus` is null for the row written at creation.

PlanEntitlementResponse.description:
An entitlement's definition and its Value on the plan: null when the stored plan has no value for
it yet (the code declares an entitlement that `seed --category CONFIGURATION` hasn't written).

additionalProperties.description: A parameter's value, by the parameter's type: a whole number (NUMBER), true or false (FLAG), one of its values (CHOICE), or an ordered list of its values, each once (LIST).

format.description: A format of the template: its code, a version (the latest when left out) and its parameters by code.

additionalProperties.description: A parameter's value, by the parameter's type: a whole number (NUMBER), true or false (FLAG), one of its values (CHOICE), or an ordered list of its values, each once (LIST).

PreviewRulesetRequest.description:
The preview's body as the API documents it: one of the template's formats with its parameters, and the changes to
the template's editable rules keyed by their dotted paths (`standings.points.win`). The endpoint reads it as
PreviewRulesetBody, so a value of the wrong shape is answered on its own field.

code.description: Stable error code, `<AREA>_<CONDITION>` (contracts/errors.json). Clients branch on it.

correlationId.description: The request's correlation ID (also the `X-Correlation-Id` response header).

errors.description: Validation failures, one per field: `field` (camelCase) and `code`.

ProfileStatus.description:
A role profile's stored states in S06 (docs/domain/state-machines.md, Registry). `SUSPENDED` comes with
discipline (S13+).

PublicAthleteProfileResponse.description: An active athlete profile: the definition's codes (labels from `GET /sports/{variant}`, AR-29).

PublicPersonPhotoResponse.description:
The photo's public routes (`GET /people/{personId}/photo?variant=`): stable paths, relative to the API's origin,
that check the person's exposure on every request.

PublicPersonResponse.description:
A person on the tenant's public site (S06 D18): only `PUBLIC` fields. For a person who isn't an adult on the
tenant's date, the display name only, plus the photo with `PHOTO` consent (ADR-0015): `nationality` is null and
`athleteProfiles` is empty.

QuotaUsageResponse.description:
One quota's usage (S04 D15): `used` of `limit` (null = unlimited) when a module measures it
(`measured`); otherwise `used` is null: not measured yet. `warning`: the tenant uses 80 % of the
limit or more.

ReadinessCheck.description: What must hold before a contest may start (S11 builds the checks; it adds others with a schema change).

RecordConsentRequest.description:
A guardian's consent (S06 D14): who gave it, to what, and on which date; `version`, when sent, must be the
person's current one. The guardian's name and contact are `PRIVATE`: kept on the record, never in the audit
trail or logs.

RedriveOutboxMessageRequest.description:
Why the message is re-driven; the audit entry records it (action audit `REQUIRED_WITH_REASON`). Kept permanently
and not redacted, so it must not contain personal data.

RemoveOverrideRequest.description:
The body of `entitlement.override.remove` (audit `REQUIRED_WITH_REASON`). The reason is kept permanently on
the override and in the audit trail and is not redacted: it must not contain personal data.

RemovePersonAliasRequest.description:
The removal of an alias (audit `REQUIRED_WITH_REASON`). The reason is kept permanently on the alias and in the
audit trail and is not redacted: it must not contain personal data.

RenewSubscriptionRequest.description:
A renewal up to `endsOn` (included). The plan, kind and windows not sent are the latest period's; a lower plan
is chosen here.

ResetPasswordRequest.description: Set a new password with the token from a reset email's link.

RevokeInvitationRequest.description: The optional body of `revoke`: `version`, when sent, must be the invitation's current one.

RevokeRoleRequest.description: The optional body of `revoke`: `version`, when sent, must be the membership's current one.

RosterLockPolicy.description: When a roster locks; Competitions (S07/S09) adds others with a schema change.

RulesetContestResponse.description: `periodSeconds` is keyed by the definition's period codes.

RulesetEligibilityResponse.description: Ages in whole years on `ageReferenceDate`; null means no limit.

RulesetLineupResponse.description: `positions` is keyed by a position code or group of the definition.

RulesetOperationsResponse.description: `officialsMinimum` is keyed by the definition's official role codes.

RulesetParameterResponse.description:
A parameter a competition may change: `min` and `max` for a number; `values` for a choice or a list
(the codes a list may hold, each once, in any order); empty otherwise. `default` is the template's value.

RulesetParameterType.description: A template parameter's type in the API; the files write `enum`, `bool`, `list`, `int`.

RulesetSportResponse.description: The sport definition the template is written for, at the exact version.

RulesetStandingsResponse.description: `tiebreakers` in the order they apply; `headToHeadReapply` is the file's `h2h_reapply`.

RulesetTemplateResponse.description:
A published ruleset template as the API shows it (docs/domain/rulesets.md): camelCase names, UPPER_SNAKE values, with
its version's hash and publication time. `parameters` are keyed by their dotted path into the rules as the files
write it (`standings.points.win`, `contest.period_seconds.FIRST_HALF`); maps keyed by codes keep the codes.
`tiebreakers` describes every tiebreaker the template lists or allows, in the catalogue's order.

RulesetValuesResponse.description: The template's rules, laid out as docs/domain/rulesets.md's snapshot.

additionalProperties.description: A parameter's value, by the parameter's type: a whole number (NUMBER), true or false (FLAG), one of its values (CHOICE), or an ordered list of its values, each once (LIST).

RulesSnapshotFormatResponse.description: The format at its exact version, with every parameter (the ones sent and the defaults) by code.

RulesSnapshotResponse.description:
An effective-rules snapshot in the API's names (docs/domain/rulesets.md): the exact sport definition, format and
template versions, the format's parameters with the defaults filled in, the rules and the snapshot's `hash`.
The hash is of the snapshot's canonical JSON (snake_case, RFC 8785), which an edition stores (S09); this answer
carries the same content in camelCase.

RulesSnapshotSportResponse.description: The sport definition the template pins, with its content hash.

SiteResponse.description:
The public site's identity: `PUBLIC` fields only. PrimaryDomain is the host the site
prefers, which may differ from the host the request came in on.

SportDefinitionResponse.description:
A published sport definition as the API shows it: the definition's content (docs/domain/sports/README.md) in the API's
names (camelCase, UPPER_SNAKE values), with its version's hash and publication time and the generic event types.
Actor roles and metadata fields stay maps keyed by their codes, as in the file.

SportMetadataFieldResponse.description: A metadata field: `values` for a choice, `min` and `max` for a number.

SportMetadataFieldType.description:
A metadata field's type in the API (`CHOICE`, `FLAG`, `NUMBER`, `TEXT`); the files write
`enum`, `bool`, `int` and `string`.

SportPeriodResponse.description: A period; `shortLabel` is the definition's short form (`1H`).

SportStatisticDerivationResponse.description: How a statistic is derived; `where` holds metadata conditions, each value as written.

StaffCapabilityRequest.description: One staff capability as sent: a variant's code, a staff role code of its definition, a qualification.

StaffCapabilityResponse.description: One thing a staff member does: a variant, a staff role of its definition and the qualification recorded.

StaffProfileRequest.description:
A staff profile's capabilities, for a new profile or replacing a profile's as a whole (S06 D12): 1–10, one per
variant and role. `version`, when sent, must be the person's current one.

StaffProfileResponse.description:
A person's work as staff (S06 D12): what they do, by variant and role (codes of the variant's definition; labels from
`GET /sports/{variant}`, AR-29).

StageType.description: The stage types of formats.md; `PLACEMENT`, `LEADERBOARD`, `HEATS` and `CARD` come later.

SubscriptionKind.description: How a period was granted; for reporting only, never affects its status or access (state-machines.md).

SubscriptionPeriodResponse.description:
One period: `startsOn` to `endsOn`, both days included. `expiringFrom` is the first day of
`EXPIRING` (after `endsOn` when the window is 0), `graceEndsOn` the last day of `GRACE`. The
cancellation fields are set together.

SubscriptionResponse.description:
A tenant's subscription as the platform sees it (S04 D16): every period, latest start first, with its status on
`today`, the tenant's date in `timeZone`. `currentPeriodId` is the period that decides access (none
without periods; with none started, the earliest scheduled one); `nextPeriodId` the earliest period that starts
after today and after the current one, never the current one. `overrides` are the tenant's entitlement overrides
with their reasons and history, unremoved first (S04 D5): platform-only. `entitlements` are every declared
entitlement's effective value today, by code, with its source (D6). `usage` is every quota's usage, as the
owning module counts it (D15; "not measured yet" when none does).

SubscriptionStatus.description:
A subscription period's status, derived from its stored dates on a given day (docs/domain/state-machines.md,
"Subscription period"); never stored.

TenantAccessMode.description: What a tenant may do, derived from its status and its current subscription period: state-machines.md.

TenantAccessPeriod.description:
The current subscription period on `/tenant/access`: its status today and its days (all included), in the
tenant's time zone. `graceEndsOn` is the last day of grace; equal to `endsOn` when the period has no grace
days. A response of its own, so a field added to Tenancy's contract for other modules doesn't change the API (#66 R4).

TenantAccessResponse.description:
A tenant's access as its owner sees it: `status`; the `accessMode` derived from it and the current
subscription period; the `reason` (null when the change needs none, such as an activation) and time
(`since`) of the change that put the tenant in its status; the tenant's `timeZone` (IANA), in which to show
`since` and the period's days; and the current period's status and days (`subscription`, null without a
period). A read-only tenant's `subscription` says why; the cancel reason is the platform's and is not shown.

TenantCapabilitiesResponse.description:
The tenant capabilities (S04 D14): `actions`, the action codes the caller may perform now (all three steps of
the decision formula), in ordinal order; `unavailable`, the actions the caller's roles grant but the tenant
can't use now, with the reason, in ordinal order; `access`, the tenant's access for the banner;
`scope`, the resource asked about, if any. Actions the roles don't grant are in neither list.

TenantEntitlementResponse.description:
One entitlement as the tenant's Subscription page shows it: its name, description, type, unit (quotas) and levels
(level entitlements, lowest first), and the tenant's value today with its source (`DEFAULT`, `PLAN` or
`OVERRIDE`).

TenantListItem.description:
A tenant in the platform list. No settings: the list runs under no tenant, and settings are tenant-owned (read one
tenant for them). `version` is the tenant row's, as in the detail.

TenantResponse.description:
A tenant as the platform API shows it: the tenant and its main settings. Read under the tenant (the settings are
tenant-owned). `version` (also the `ETag`), `createdAt` and `updatedAt` are the tenant row's
only: a settings change doesn't change them, so the same `ETag` can come with different settings. Send
`version` back with a change to make it fail with `409 TENANT_CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT` if someone else changed
the tenant first. The settings have their own version at `/api/admin/v1/tenant/settings`.

TenantSettingsResponse.description:
A tenant's settings as the admin API shows them. `version` (also the `ETag`) and `updatedAt` are the
settings row's, not the tenant's: send `version` back with a change to make it fail with
`409 TENANT_CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT` if someone else changed the settings first.

TenantSportResponse.description:
A published variant at its latest version: `enabledSince` is when its current enablement began (null when it
isn't enabled).

TenantSportsResponse.description:
Every published sport variant and whether the tenant has it enabled (S05 D15). `sportQuota` is the
`MAX_ENABLED_SPORTS` usage for those who may read the subscription (`tenant.subscription.read`), else null.

TenantSubscriptionPeriod.description:
A period's plan (code and name), kind and status today, and its days, all included: `expiringFrom` is the first
day of `EXPIRING` (after `endsOn` when the window is 0), `graceEndsOn` the last day of `GRACE`.

TenantSubscriptionResponse.description:
A tenant's subscription as its members see it (S04 D15): `today` in the tenant's `timeZone`; the
`current` period (the one that decides access; null without periods; with none started, the earliest
scheduled one) and the `next` one (the earliest that starts after today and after the current one, never the
current one); every declared entitlement's effective value with its source; and every quota's usage. No override
reasons, cancel reasons or who made a change: those are the platform's.

TimeZoneResponse.description: An IANA time zone: its ID as `code` (`Africa/Kampala`) and its country; no country for `Etc/UTC`.

UnavailableActionResponse.description:
An action the caller's roles grant that the tenant can't use now. `code` is the refusal the request would get
first: `TENANT_READ_ONLY` (step 1) or `ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED` (step 2). For `ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED`,
`entitlement` is the entitlement the action names and `plans` the active plans, in rank order, that include
it (empty when none does); both are null for `TENANT_READ_ONLY`.

UpdateAthleteProfileRequest.description:
An athlete profile's details, replaced as a whole (a field left out is cleared); the variant never changes.
`version`, when sent, must be the person's current one.

UpdatePersonRequest.description:
A person's whole biodata, replacing what is stored (S06 D8): a field left out is cleared. External identifiers and
aliases change through their own actions. `checkToken` and `overrideReason` are
needed only when the names, date of birth or nationalities change; `version`, when sent, must be the person's
current one.

UpdateTenantProfileRequest.description:
The profile fields to change; a missing or null field stays as it is. The slug and the status can't be changed here
(unknown members are rejected). `version`, when sent, must be the tenant's current version.

UpdateTenantSettingsRequest.description:
The settings to change; a missing or null key stays as it is. Only these keys exist: any other key, or a value of
the wrong type, is named in `errors`. `version`, when sent, must be the settings' current version.

VenueDuplicateCandidateResponse.description:
A venue that looks like the one checked (S07 D13): enough to recognise it and open it. `status` marks an
archived one.

VenueDuplicateEvidenceCode.description: Why a venue looks like the one checked (S07 D13).

code.description: Stable error code, `<AREA>_<CONDITION>` (contracts/errors.json). Clients branch on it.

correlationId.description: The request's correlation ID (also the `X-Correlation-Id` response header).

errors.description: Validation failures, one per field: `field` (camelCase) and `code`.

VenueDuplicateReviewProblem.description:
The Problem Details of a venue create refused with `422` (S07 D13), for the OpenAPI document and the generated
client: `candidates` is present only with `VENUE_DUPLICATE_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, the venues the warning found,
strongest first.

VenueResponse.description:
A venue as the admin reads it (S07 D19). Every field is one the public reads may show (D16) but the version.
Surfaces and variants keep the order they were sent in; variants are codes, labelled from the definitions (AR-29).

VenueStatus.description: A venue's states (docs/domain/state-machines.md, Registry; S07 D12). The transitions come with S07-T1b.

VenueSurface.description: A playing surface a venue has (S07 D3). Generic codes: none names a sport (AR-11).

VenueType.description: What kind of place a venue is (S07 D3). Generic codes: none names a sport (AR-11).

WithdrawConsentRequest.description:
Withdrawing scopes of a consent (audit `REQUIRED_WITH_REASON`). The reason is kept permanently on the record and
in the audit trail and is not redacted: it must not contain personal data.
